specs.value: Foam, Bio-Foam, Biomax, Carbon Foam, media bags
3-year official manufacturer warranty (stated for the FX range listing)

fits.fact: Aimed at large tanks of roughly 400–1,500 L.
Can be used on freshwater or marine tanks; for marine, pick media to suit.
Total rated capacity is up to 1,500 L, so it suits big community, monster-fish or heavily stocked tanks.
The FX6 holds more foam than the FX4, which gives it more biological capacity for heavy stocking.
One estimate: about 0.2 cu ft of 30 ppi foam in an FX6 supports roughly 1 lb of fish, and adding similar media in the baskets raises that to about 2 lb.
For smaller tanks, the FX4 (up to 1,000 L) or FX2 (up to 750 L) is a better-sized and cheaper choice.

usage.fact: Put the canister at least 20 cm below the tank bottom so it gets good water pressure.
Set the intake low near the tank bottom and keep it away from the outlet so filtered water isn't sucked straight back in.
Fill the canister with water before the first start. It starts by itself when plugged in, but give it a few minutes to push out the air.
Never run it dry, because the pump can burn out.
Check the AquaStop valves regularly for leaks. They let you cut off the flow for maintenance without taking the hoses apart.
The shop recommends cleaning every 1–2 months, depending on how heavily the tank is stocked.
The Smart Pump is said to restart by itself after a power cut and to adjust its output.
An independent guide says to clean the foam only when it clogs, not on a fixed schedule, because cleaning strips bacteria that take a month or more to recover.
The same guide advises leaving the trays in, swapping the Biomax ceramic rings for better media, and skipping monthly carbon changes.
Some owners say the impeller and its housing need cleaning about every 3 months, or the pump may not start or may get loud.

issues.fact: Some new units are reported as very noisy. Often the cause is debris in the impeller or clogged media, and cleaning fixes it.
Air leaking in at the hose connections can cause noise and slow water loss. Tightening the connections fixed it.
The stock ribbed hose is criticised for getting pinholes, cracks and tears, and its unusual size makes replacement fittings hard to find.
The one-direction motor depends on a starter that can fail, so the impeller hums but doesn't spin.
Some buyers report leaks from the impeller housing within months, plus slow warranty and customer-service responses from Fluval.
Specs differ by voltage: the 230 V unit is listed at 41 W and the US 120 V unit at 43 W, and sources disagree on head height (2.1 m vs 3.3 m).
The 3,500 L/h figure is the pump's output with no load. Flow through the media is about 2,130 L/h.
Stock in Vietnam is patchy: one shop shows the FX6 as sold out and another only gives the price on request.

alternatives.why: Same Smart Pump design for less money (about 9.75M VND). It is rated for tanks up to 1,000 L, uses 30 W and is smaller, so it suits mid-size tanks better.
Cheapest model in the range (about 7.85M VND), for tanks up to 750 L.
A European rival with a larger 8 L media volume for tanks up to 850 L, drawing 32 W. Its flow is lower (1,550 L/h). I didn't confirm a Vietnamese shop price.
